entries.why: Covers the guards the port adds to orch/store.ts: nested-paren status rows, leading-dash branch names, single-line table cells, frontier SHAs from exact branch refs, and colour and hyperlink codes in gt output, injecting the fake gt through the store's gt option instead of rewriting PATH and giving the CLI only PATH and ORCH_STORE instead of the whole environment. For the stale-lock takeover it races two processes for a stale lock to show only one replaces it, refuses every writer, forced or not, while a live writer holds the takeover claim, pauses a second process at its unlink of the lock to show a forced writer is refused mid-takeover, pauses a holder at the unlink of its release to show a forced writer is refused there too, kills one there to show the next writer clears its claim, removes the lock there to show the takeover carries on, and pauses one after it has listed a dead claimant to show it leaves alone a claim made since. Kills a writer after every lock call, with and without a stale lock, to show the next writer gets in, fails the hard link to show the exclusive open still refuses a live lock, plants and removes a rival lock between a failed create and the read to show the create is retried, and points the lock at a missing file to show the retry ends. Expects unit add to return ids and tracks as written, round-trips unit cells and inbox pointers that start with a formula or quote character and pins their quoted form on disk, reads rows written before the quote was stripped without dropping a leading quote, and times out gt log and gt info against a gt that ignores SIGTERM, with a budget a saturated machine can meet.

source_review.semantic_delta: **Adapt.** Comparator tests inject `gt` through the store option and exercise takeover races, killing writers at lock transitions, lock creation/retry failures, timeout behavior, and formula/quote TSV round-trips. Target helper modifies `PATH` and its tests cover basic stale/live lock behavior, but not those comparator safety cases (comparator test lines 1–200 plus later lock cases; target test lines 1–180, 335–374).
source_review.check_or_gap: Target `orch/orch.test.ts` covers basic store operations, stale-lock recovery, and forced takeover. It does **not** cover the comparator’s race-proof takeover protocol, kill-at-transition cases, timeout, or quoted-cell round-trip.

entries.why: Adds guards for temp-file cleanup, single-line status table cells, nested-paren gt status rows, leading-dash branch names, and frontier SHAs resolved from exact local branch refs, runs gt and git without an env override and strips terminal control sequences from gt output instead of setting NO_COLOR, and takes the gt path as an open option so tests can inject a fake. Serializes stale-lock takeovers behind a claim directory that holds one file named for the claimant's pid, staged under a private name and renamed into place. A live claim refuses every other writer, forced or not, and the next writer removes a dead claimant's file by name before it claims. Inside the claim the takeover re-reads the lock, refuses when the holder changed, and carries on when the lock is already gone. The release reads and unlinks its own lock behind the same claim, so a forced takeover cannot replace the lock between the two, and stages a new claim until a live claimant finishes or dies. Creates the lock by writing the pid to a private file and hard-linking it into place, so a writer killed mid-create cannot leave a lock with no pid in it, and falls back to an exclusive open where the link fails for any reason other than an existing lock. Creates the lock again, twice at most, when it vanishes between a failed create and the read of its holder, and reports a lock it cannot read as held by an unknown pid. Quotes a cell that starts with a spreadsheet formula character or a quote only when writing a TSV or an inbox pointer, and strips that quote when reading one, so ids and branches round-trip unchanged. A row written before this change keeps a leading quote unless another quote or a formula character follows it; that is the shape the store writes, so such a row loses its first quote on read. Bounds each gt call with a timeout that kills gt with SIGKILL and that the gtTimeoutMs open option overrides.

source_review.semantic_delta: **GAP (#434).** Comparator adds serialized stale-lock takeover with claimant directory, hard-link lock creation, bounded retries, release serialized against takeover, formula/quote-safe TSV cells, VT-control stripping, exact branch-ref SHA resolution, injectable `gt`, and bounded `gt` calls. Target uses a plain pid lock and `open`-based acquisition; `cleanCell` protects formula prefixes but not quote-prefix round-tripping (target lines 17–20, 296–299; comparator lines 17–24 and store lock/frontier sections). Comparator tests specify the missing boundaries; the target store does not implement them.
